# Statement → prediction, checked without a server.
#
# The other half of the acceptance is the oracle in oracle_integration_test.go,
# which runs each statement against a real PostgreSQL and reads pg_locks. This
# file is not a substitute for it: a corpus written from the same reading of the
# documentation as the rules can only prove that the author was consistent.
# What it is for is the cases the oracle cannot reach — the version-dependent
# rules, the offline answer, and the forms that cannot run inside the
# transaction the oracle rolls back.
#
# Syntax: "version:" sets the server version for the cases below it, "sql:"
# starts a case, and each "want:" line is one expected prediction:
#
#     want: <relation> | <LOCK LEVEL> | <flags>
#
# where flags is any of "rewrite" and "scan", space separated. A relation of "-"
# means the prediction names none.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- PostgreSQL 17
version: 170000

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email text
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN score int DEFAULT 0 NOT NULL
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN created_at timestamptz DEFAULT now()
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN k uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN r double precision DEFAULT random()
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite

# An unrecognised function is assumed volatile, because the pessimistic answer
# is the one that cannot cause an outage.
sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN x int DEFAULT my_extension_thing()
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN total int GENERATED ALWAYS AS (a + b) STORED
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN code text UNIQUE
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE public.orders ALTER COLUMN status TYPE text
want: public.orders | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: ALTER TABLE orders ALTER COLUMN total TYPE numeric USING total::numeric
want: orders | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email SET NOT NULL
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email DROP NOT NULL
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email SET DEFAULT 'x'
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE users ALTER COLUMN email SET STATISTICS 1000
want: users | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT positive CHECK (total > 0)
want: orders | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT positive CHECK (total > 0) NOT VALID
want: orders | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE orders VALIDATE CONSTRAINT positive
want: orders | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE | scan

# Both tables, which is the surprise this package exists to print.
sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users (id)
want: orders | SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE | scan
want: users | SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE orders ADD CONSTRAINT fk FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES public.users (id) NOT VALID
want: orders | SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE
want: public.users | SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT u UNIQUE (email)
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD CONSTRAINT u UNIQUE USING INDEX ix_users_email
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE users SET UNLOGGED
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: ALTER TABLE users SET TABLESPACE fast
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: ALTER TABLE users SET (fillfactor = 70)
want: users | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE

# One statement, several actions: the strongest claim per table wins, and the
# reason shown is the rewrite rather than the lock.
sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN a int, ADD COLUMN b uuid DEFAULT gen_random_uuid()
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite

sql: ALTER TABLE parts ATTACH PARTITION parts_2026 FOR VALUES FROM ('2026-01-01') TO ('2027-01-01')
want: parts | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE
want: parts_2026 | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: ALTER TABLE parts DETACH PARTITION parts_2026 CONCURRENTLY
want: parts | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE
want: parts_2026 | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE

sql: CREATE INDEX ix ON users (email)
want: users | SHARE | scan

sql: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix ON users (email)
want: users | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE | scan

# The ON of a partial index predicate must not be mistaken for the ON of the
# table, which is why the cursor skips parenthesised text whole.
sql: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix ON public.users (lower(email)) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
want: public.users | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: DROP INDEX ix
want: ix | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY ix
want: ix | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE

sql: REINDEX TABLE users
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: REINDEX TABLE CONCURRENTLY users
want: users | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: VACUUM FULL users
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: VACUUM (FULL, ANALYZE) users
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: VACUUM ANALYZE users
want: users | SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: CLUSTER users USING ix
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW mv
want: mv | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite scan

sql: REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY mv
want: mv | EXCLUSIVE | scan

sql: TRUNCATE orders
want: orders | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: DROP TABLE IF EXISTS old_sessions
want: old_sessions | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: LOCK TABLE users IN SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE MODE
want: users | SHARE ROW EXCLUSIVE

sql: LOCK TABLE users
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES ('a')
want: users | ROW EXCLUSIVE

sql: SELECT count(*) FROM users
want: users | ACCESS SHARE

sql: SELECT id FROM users FOR UPDATE
want: users | ROW SHARE

sql: CREATE TABLE t (id int)
want: - | none

sql: COMMENT ON TABLE users IS 'people'
want: - | none

# A quoted identifier keeps its case; an unquoted one is folded.
sql: ALTER TABLE "Users" ADD COLUMN x int
want: Users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: ALTER TABLE MyTable ADD COLUMN x int
want: mytable | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

# Comments, including nested block comments, must not confuse the reader.
sql: /* outer /* inner */ still a comment */ ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE

sql: THIS IS NOT SQL
want: - | unknown

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- PostgreSQL 10
# Before 11 every DEFAULT on a new column rewrote the table, and before 12
# ATTACH PARTITION locked the parent outright.
version: 100000

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN score int DEFAULT 0
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite

sql: ALTER TABLE parts ATTACH PARTITION parts_2026 FOR VALUES FROM (1) TO (2)
want: parts | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
want: parts_2026 | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | scan

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- no server
# Offline, a version-dependent rule gives the answer that was true before the
# version that improved it. Reading it optimistically would turn the rewrite of
# a large table into a line that said it was cheap.
version: 0

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN score int DEFAULT 0
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE | rewrite

sql: ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email text
want: users | ACCESS EXCLUSIVE
